brief: JPM's afternoon briefing centers on a Financials selloff (XLF -2%) against a continuing AI/semis rally (SOXX +2.4%, DRAM +3.3%), both attributed to the return of the post-Meta Muse +Semis/-AI Vulnerable trade. Financials specialist O'Dwyer argues there is no clean fundamental reason for the bank move: the narrative that Muse/agentic AI threatens bank funding economics doesn't hold, since Muse itself is seen as untrustworthy; instead, consensus names (C, MS, GS, USB) dominating volume while regionals and LAZ/JEF outperform reads as a positioning unwind, not a re-rating, so he wants to fade the selloff, favoring MS, PNC, FITB. Trading co-head Adler frames Muse as agents superseding chatbots, favoring META/GOOGL/AAPL on trust, reducing reliance on frontier chips (a headwind for neoclouds), and broadening the AI trade toward CPU/memory/storage away from GPUs, while turning cautious on frontier-model economics near RSI. Oil fell 1.2% despite Iran's conditional offer to reopen the Strait within seven days and Rubio's 60-70% flow comment, since Trump reiterated a peace deal may wait until after the midterms. Fedspeak (Barkin, echoes of Warsh) raises hike risk. JPM stays Tactically Cautious/Neutral into the Fed, bullish only on lower oil/yields, keeping +Tech/-RTY and a Latam long.
